errors.quote: introduced jointly by Gauss and Legendre in their 1805 paper
errors.why: Legendre published least squares in 1805; Gauss claimed it later, in 1809. There was no joint paper.
The gradient is $+2A^\top(A\beta - y)$. The sign does not change where it vanishes, so the normal equations survive.
$A^\top A$ is invertible only when the columns of $A$ are independent: here, when the $x_i$ are not all equal.

errors.quote: we refit the same points with the same code and check that the slope comes out the same
errors.why: Running deterministic code twice on the same input always agrees; it checks nothing. Compare with a case whose answer is known, or with another method.

judgement: Not as written: the uniqueness claim needs the columns of $A$ independent, which is the error that changes a conclusion.
